 Pistons Notes: Jenkins, Lineup, Collins, Duren, Okorie
 By Dana Gauruder |
 at November 10, 2026 7:55 pm 
 Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff tweaked his starting lineup on Monday, inserting guard Daniss Jenkins in place of big man Paul Reed . The move paid dividends, as Jenkins supplied 22 points, eight assists, six rebounds and four steals in a 122-111 win over Washington. That snapped a two-game slide and improved Detroit’s record to 7-3.
 Bickerstaff indicated he may decide on his fifth starter on a game-by-game basis until Jalen Duren returns from his hamstring injury.
 “I think DJ has earned more with the way that he’s sparked us coming off of the bench,” Bickerstaff said of Jenkins. “We talked about our starts and how we thought we could improve those starts. Matchups dictated some of that also. Being able to have him go up against Trae Young , and then put AT ( Ausar Thompson ) on AJ (Dybantsa) , I thought that matchup would be good for us as well. So, trying to find a spark to start, but again, the matchups played a part in it also.” 
 Duncan Robinson , who also scored 22 points, said Jenkins is the team’s spark-plug.
 “We’re tough when Daniss is aggressive like that. We love to see him be an aggressive play-maker for himself and others,” Robinson said.
 Jenkins will be eligible for restricted free agency after this season.
 Here’s more on the Pistons:
 John Collins , the team’s biggest free agent acquisition this offseason, had his best game of the young season on Monday, with 24 points and 10 rebounds. Collins was the center in the smaller lineup and Bickerstaff said the big man will see action at both power positions. “Yeah, I mean he was involved, and I think that’s the most important thing for him, and that’s what we’re trying to find—that balance when he’s at the four versus the five,” Bickerstaff said. “How [do] we still get him involved in some of the action? Throughout his career when he’s been in the pick-and-roll situations, he’s really good at playing in the pocket and finishing, and then obviously he has the capability of knocking down shots. So again, we’re learning and we’ll figure it out eventually. But [we] are just trying to find out how we use guys best.” 
 Duren’s interior presence is still missed despite the team’s record, Detroit News beat writer Coty M. Davis opines, noting that Washington’s Anthony Davis erupted for 44 points and 13 rebounds against Detroit. Without Duren to collect rebounds, the Pistons averaged 42.3 rebounds over the last eight games, ranking 18th in the league. They’ve allowed opponents to average 12.4 offensive rebounds per game during that stretch. “We are trying our best to make up what (Duren) brings to us every night,” Cade Cunningham said. “Being on the glass while still trying to get paint points. Obviously, we haven’t done anywhere near as well as we do when he is with us, but the togetherness and trying to cover for each other have been there. That has allowed us to win games.” 
 First-round pick Ebuka Okorie hasn’t gotten much playing time so far, with Cunningham and Jenkins eating up most of the minutes at the point. But Okorie got a chance to play some fourth-quarter minutes on Monday and he contributed five points in six minutes. “He’s just a hooper. You can tell he loves the game, works hard at it,” Cunningham said, per Jacob Richman of MLive.com . “You can tell he’s just itching over there for his moment. So whenever his number is called, he’s ready and he’s excited about it and he goes out there and plays like it.”
